title: Fifteen Medals for Ireland at BMAF Track & Field Championships
summary: A stellar weekend for Irish masters athletes at the BMAF Track & Field Championships in Derby — 15 medals across sprints, hurdles, middle distance and field events.
content:
While the mountain runners were conquering Romania, another group of Irish masters athletes were delivering outstanding performances at the BMAF Track & Field Championships in Derby this past weekend — bringing home **15 medals** across a wide range of events.

## The Standout Performances

**Anne Gilshinan** (W60) was the star of the Irish contingent, winning **Gold** in the 800m (2:27.85) and **Gold** in the 1500m (5:02.01) — a magnificent double on the track.

**Tom O'Brien** (M55) was equally impressive in the field, taking **Gold** in the High Jump (1.55m) and **Silver** in the Long Jump (5.24m).

**Damian Crawford** (M55) won **Gold** in the Javelin, adding to what was a superb weekend for the M55 age group.

**Ger Cremin** (M45) won **Gold** in the 110m Hurdles — finishing 3rd overall in the combined M35-45 race but claiming the M45 age group title with a time of 17.09.

**Ciara Burrows** (W40) had a brilliant weekend in the throws, winning **Bronze in both the Discus and the Shot Put** in the W40 age group.

**Noelle O'Regan** (W35) took a fine **Silver** in the 400m, running 1:01.20, while **Lynsey Glover** (W35) won **Silver** in the Weight Throw.

**Keith Pollard** (M45) earned two bronze medals — in the 200m (23.88) and the 400m (54.15).

**Robert Bruce-Brand** (M55) claimed **Bronze** in the 400m M55 (58.50), **Eoghan Murphy** (M35) took **Bronze** in the 800m (2:22.45), and **Alison Beck** (W45) rounded off the haul with **Bronze** in the High Jump (1.40m).

## An Irish Masters Weekend to Remember

Taken together with the EMORRC results from Romania, this was one of the finest weekends Irish masters athletics has produced in a long time — medals across mountain running and track & field, with athletes competing from M35 through to W60 age groups.

The depth and quality on show is a real statement of intent for Irish masters athletics, and a tremendous encouragement as we build towards the European Masters Athletics Championships Non-Stadia in Galway in May 2028.

We hope to see many of these athletes — and many more — on the start line in Galway.

*The EMACNS Galway 2028 Organising Committee*

title: Irish Masters Shine at EMORRC 2026 Râșnov
summary: Ireland's masters athletes delivered a brilliant weekend in the mountains of Romania — 10 medals across three days at the European Masters Off Road Running Championships.
content:
Ireland's masters running community had a weekend to remember in Râșnov, Romania, as athletes from across the country competed at the European Masters Off Road Running Championships (EMORRC) 2026 — and came home with 10 medals.

## The Headline Results

**Des Crowe** (M65) was magnificent across both race days, winning **Gold** in the Vertical Race on Friday and adding a **Bronze** in the Classic Up&Down on Sunday. A superb double for one of Ireland's most experienced masters mountain runners.

**James Kevan** (M35) produced a commanding performance in Sunday's Classic Up&Down, taking **Gold** in an impressive 47:04. A first European masters medal and what a way to get it.

**Brendan Forrester** (M40) showed real class in both events — **Bronze** in Friday's Vertical Race and **Silver** in Sunday's Classic Up&Down. A remarkable weekend's racing.

**Joe Gough** (M70) added **Silver** in the Classic Up&Down and was part of the triumphant **M70 team that won Gold** in Sunday's event — Joe, Matthew Alexander and Peter Bell combining for 15 points and the team title.

**Philip Goss** (M40) took **Bronze** in the Classic Up&Down, while **Paul Faulkner** (M50) claimed **Bronze** in Friday's Vertical Race.

The M70s were busy all weekend — Matthew Alexander, Gerry Brady and Peter Bell claimed **Team Silver** in Friday's Vertical Race before regrouping for Sunday's team gold.

## Full Irish Medal Table — EMORRC 2026

| Medal | Athlete | Category | Race |
|---|---|---|---|
| 🥇 Gold | Des Crowe | M65 | Vertical Race (Fri) |
| 🥇 Gold | James Kevan | M35 | Classic Up&Down (Sun) |
| 🥈 Silver | Brendan Forrester | M40 | Classic Up&Down (Sun) |
| 🥈 Silver | Joe Gough | M70 | Classic Up&Down (Sun) |
| 🥇 Team Gold | Gough / Alexander / Bell | M70 | Classic Up&Down (Sun) |
| 🥈 Team Silver | Alexander / Brady / Bell | M70 | Vertical Race (Fri) |
| 🥉 Bronze | Brendan Forrester | M40 | Vertical Race (Fri) |
| 🥉 Bronze | Paul Faulkner | M50 | Vertical Race (Fri) |
| 🥉 Bronze | Philip Goss | M40 | Classic Up&Down (Sun) |
| 🥉 Bronze | Des Crowe | M65 | Classic Up&Down (Sun) |

## The Bigger Picture

Fourteen Irish athletes competed across the three race days — a significant and committed squad to travel to Romania for a mountain running championship. The championship format — Friday Vertical Race, Saturday Long Distance, Sunday Classic Up&Down — tested endurance, technical ability and sheer mountain running grit.

This is exactly the kind of event that Galway 2028 will be delivering for masters athletes across Europe. We hope many of the athletes who raced in Râșnov this weekend will be with us on the Wild Atlantic Way in May 2028.

Comhghairdeas le gach duine — congratulations to all.

*The EMACNS Galway 2028 Organising Committee*

title: A Brilliant Championship — Well Done Râșnov!
summary: The European Masters Off Road Running Championships in Râșnov, Romania wrapped up this weekend — a superb event and a wonderful blueprint for masters athletics done right.
content:
The European Masters Off Road Running Championships (EMORRC) concluded this weekend in Râșnov, Romania, and what a championship it was.

Over three days, more than 400 masters athletes from across Europe took on the mountains of Transylvania — the Vertical Race, Long Distance, and Classic Up&Down — in what organisers Run Transylvania delivered as a seamless, atmospheric and genuinely memorable event. Stunning scenery, warm hospitality and serious competition: everything a masters athletics championship should be.

From the Galway 2028 organising team, a heartfelt congratulations to everyone involved in making EMORRC 2026 such a success — the organising committee, the volunteers, and the people of Râșnov who welcomed so many athletes and their families to their beautiful town.

Events like this are an inspiration as we build towards the European Masters Athletics Championships Non-Stadia here in Galway in May 2028. We hope many of the athletes who raced in Romania this weekend will be lining up on the Wild Atlantic Way in two years' time.

Maith sibh go léir — well done to all!

*The EMACNS Galway 2028 Organising Committee*

title: Welcome to EMACNS Galway 2028
summary: We are delighted to announce that Galway will host the European Masters Athletics Championships Non-Stadia in May 2028. Planning is underway and we look forward to welcoming masters athletes from across Europe.
content:
We are thrilled to officially launch the website for EMACNS Galway 2028 — the European Masters Athletics Championships Non-Stadia, coming to Galway, Ireland in May 2028.

Planning is well underway and we look forward to welcoming masters athletes from over 20 nations to one of Ireland's most vibrant and beautiful cities.

Over the coming months we will be sharing updates on the event programme, venues, accommodation and everything you need to know to make the most of your time in Galway.

Stay tuned — and if you'd like to volunteer or discuss sponsorship opportunities, please visit the relevant sections of this website.

*The EMACNS Galway 2028 Organising Committee*
